title: Summa Theologiae I, question 2
author: Thomas Aquinas · New Advent edition
note: Read the objections as well as the replies. Aquinas argues from effects to God; our contingency outline is an introductory reconstruction, not a quotation of his Five Ways. Limited use: causation and dependence in I, q.2, a.3, alongside Sproul. This does not endorse Aquinas's account of justification, merit or ecclesial authority.

title: Festal Letter 39
author: Athanasius of Alexandria · New Advent edition
note: A historical witness to the books Athanasius received, including the 27 books of the New Testament. One bishop's list is evidence within a wider history of reception. Used for the New Testament list in section 5, not as our standard for the Old Testament canon.

title: On Grace and Free Will, chapter 17
author: Augustine of Hippo · New Advent edition
note: Limited use: faith is God's gift and good works follow it. Augustine predates the Reformation. This citation does not equate his entire account of justification with the Reformed confession.

title: The Not-self Characteristic
author: SN 22:59 · Thanissaro Bhikkhu
role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
note: The five aggregates are examined as impermanent and not-self. Do not reduce this passage to the slogan that people do not exist.

title: Setting the Wheel of Dhamma in Motion
author: SN 56:11 · Thanissaro Bhikkhu
role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
note: The four noble truths and the eightfold path. A Pali discourse in Thanissaro Bhikkhu’s translation; this collection is scoped to these early discourses, not every Buddhist school.

title: Of Justification by Faith
author: John Calvin · Institutes III.11, Ligonier excerpt
note: For forgiveness and Christ's righteousness received through faith alone, distinguished from the believer's renewal and works. Do not treat faith itself as a meritorious achievement.

title: Institutes I.7: Scripture and the Spirit
author: John Calvin · Beveridge translation, CCEL
note: Sections 1–5 locate Scripture's authority in God and assurance in the Spirit's witness. The church receives God's Word; it does not confer authority on it.

title: Institutes II.3: the corruption of human nature
author: John Calvin · Beveridge translation, CCEL
note: Sections 3–4 distinguish God's restraint of sin and gifts in civic life from an inwardly righteous heart. Used alongside Romans 3, not to deny the benefit of an unbeliever's kindness.

title: Common Grace
author: Ligonier Ministries · theological guide
note: Used for providential kindness, the restraint of evil and civic virtue. Common grace must be distinguished from the regenerating grace that brings sinners to faith.

title: The Concept of God — full transcript
author: William Lane Craig & Shabir Ally · hosted by Reasonable Faith
role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
note: McMaster University, March 2002. A Christian–Muslim exchange about the concept of God; neither speaker represents every member of his tradition. Documentary use only: Craig is not a Reformed doctrinal authority for this library. Assess the arguments against Scripture and the doctrinal basis stated here.

title: Hoax or History? — full transcript
author: William Lane Craig & Shabir Ally · hosted by Reasonable Faith
role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
note: McGill University, February 2009. The transcript preserves the exchange; the questions in our study guide are editorial prompts, not quotations from the speakers. Documentary use only: Craig is not a Reformed doctrinal authority for this library. Assess the arguments against Scripture and the doctrinal basis stated here.

title: Does God Exist? — full transcript
author: William Lane Craig & Christopher Hitchens · hosted by Reasonable Faith
role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
note: Hosted by Craig's organization, with both speakers' contributions. Read the complete exchange and distinguish a speaker's assertion from demonstrated evidence. Documentary use only: Craig is not a Reformed doctrinal authority for this library. Assess the arguments against Scripture and the doctrinal basis stated here.

title: The Nicene Creed
author: Historic Christian confession · Church of England text
note: A historic confession of Christian belief. It identifies the doctrine being defended; it is not independent historical evidence for every claim.

title: Who Can Be Against Us?
author: Sinclair Ferguson · Things Unseen, Ligonier Ministries
note: For assurance grounded in the Father giving his Son (Romans 8:31–32), rather than in interpreting every changing circumstance as a verdict on God's love.

title: Guidelines for Separation
author: Sinclair Ferguson · Ligonier Ministries
note: For biblical discipline that takes sin seriously and seeks restoration. Not used as legal advice or as a reason to silence someone reporting harm.

title: Bhagavad Gita 2.47
author: Bhagavad Gita · Swami Mukundananda
role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
note: Action without attachment to its fruits. Read the verse in its dialogue with Arjuna and distinguish the primary verse from the translator’s commentary.

title: Bhagavad Gita 18.66
author: Bhagavad Gita · Swami Mukundananda
role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
note: Krishna’s invitation to take refuge in him. This text prevents a simplistic description of Hindu liberation as merely earning merit; compare interpretations within Hindu traditions.

title: Bhagavad Gita 2.20
author: Bhagavad Gita · Swami Mukundananda
role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
note: The enduring self, in Swami Mukundananda’s translation. This devotional interpretation does not represent every Hindu school.

title: Declaration of Modern Humanism
author: Humanists International · 2022
role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
note: An organization's own account of humanist ethics, reason and meaning. It does not speak for every atheist or secular person.

title: The NT canon was not decided at Nicaea
author: Michael J. Kruger · Canon Fodder
note: For distinguishing the church's recognition of Scripture from a council creating its authority. Discusses the surviving evidence rather than attributing the canon to Nicaea.

title: Penal Substitution
author: Ligonier Ministries · Tabletalk devotional
note: For Christ bearing the penalty of sin as substitute. Other biblical descriptions of the atonement complement this truth rather than displace it.

title: Qur’an 112:1–4
author: Qur’an · Quran.com translations
role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
note: An Islamic primary text on God's oneness and incomparability. Compare translations and commentary; an English rendering is not the Arabic text itself.

title: Qur’an 15:9
author: Qur’an · Mustafa Khattab, The Clear Quran
role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
note: The promise to preserve the Reminder. A textual promise and the historical evidence of transmission are distinct questions.

title: Qur’an 33:40
author: Qur’an · Mustafa Khattab, The Clear Quran
role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
note: Muhammad described as messenger and seal of the prophets. This is the text’s claim; demonstrating a prophetic claim requires further examination.

title: Qur’an 3:59
author: Qur’an · Mustafa Khattab, The Clear Quran
role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
note: Jesus and Adam compared through God’s creative command. This passage records the Qur’anic comparison; it does not confess the eternal divine Son.

title: Qur’an 39:53–54
author: Qur’an · Mustafa Khattab, The Clear Quran
role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
note: Read the promise of mercy in 39:53 together with the call to repent and submit in 39:54. Do not describe Islam as lacking divine mercy.

title: Qur’an 4:157–158
author: Qur’an · Quran.com translations
role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
note: Start at 4:157 and continue to 4:158. Distinguish the wording from later explanations of the crucifixion.

title: Qur’an 4:163–165
author: Qur’an · Mustafa Khattab, The Clear Quran
role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
note: Revelation to Muhammad placed alongside earlier prophets. Read through 4:165 for the stated purpose of the messengers.

title: Qur’an 4:171
author: Qur’an · Quran.com translations
role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
note: A primary passage addressing Jesus and the language of three. Read its whole statement rather than an isolated phrase.

title: Qur’an 53:38–42
author: Qur’an · Mustafa Khattab, The Clear Quran
role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
note: Personal responsibility, endeavour, recompense and return to God. Read alongside passages on mercy; these verses alone do not exhaust Islamic accounts of salvation.

title: Qur’an 5:48
author: Qur’an · Mustafa Khattab, The Clear Quran
role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
note: The Qur’an describes its relationship to earlier Scripture and calls for judgment by what God revealed. Translation of muhaymin varies; this entry uses the named translation without collapsing questions about earlier texts.

title: Codex Sinaiticus: the manuscript
author: Codex Sinaiticus Project
role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
note: The project's introduction dates the Greek manuscript to the middle of the fourth century and describes its corrections. Follow its manuscript viewer to inspect the witness itself.

title: The Self-Existent God
author: R. C. Sproul · Ligonier Ministries
note: For God's underived existence and the distinction between being self-existent and causing oneself. This argument does not by itself establish the Trinity or the gospel.

title: Difference or Contradiction?
author: R. C. Sproul · Ligonier Ministries
note: For distinguishing genuinely incompatible assertions from complementary accounts. A possible reconciliation must not be presented as a demonstrated historical event.

title: Have we lost the image of God?
author: R. C. Sproul · Ligonier Ministries
note: Explains the continuing image of God after the fall and the difference between total and utter depravity. Image-bearing does not mean innocence or saving righteousness.

title: Does the Bible Have Errors?
author: R. C. Sproul · Ligonier Ministries
note: For the truthfulness of Scripture because its divine author is truthful. This is distinct from claiming that every copy, translation or proposed interpretation is error-free.

title: A Supernatural Faith
author: R. C. Sproul · Ligonier Ministries
note: For the indispensable place of God's supernatural acts in Christianity. This does not authenticate every modern miracle claim.

title: The Christian and Science
author: R. C. Sproul · Ligonier Ministries
note: Used for the unity of truth and the fallibility of human interpretations of Scripture and nature. It is not a source for a particular scientific measurement or model.

title: From Suffering to Glory, Part 2
author: R. C. Sproul · Romans sermon, Ligonier Ministries
note: For Romans 8:28 and Genesis 50:20: God's good purpose and human evil intentions can concern the same event. The promise belongs to those who love God; it does not make evil good.

title: What Is Catechism? · Commentary prolegomena
author: Zacharias Ursinus
note: An introductory excerpt from the Heidelberg Catechism commentary, not the complete commentary. Sections III–IV explain the distinction between law and gospel and the order of misery, deliverance and gratitude.

title: Westminster Confession of Faith
author: Westminster Assembly · OPC text
note: Our subordinate doctrinal standard for these guides. Citations specify chapter and paragraph. Scripture judges the confession itself (1.10); the confession does not replace Scripture.

title: Sennacherib 022
author: RINAP 3 · Q003496 · annotated English edition, 2012
role: Ancient royal account, accessed through a modern scholarly edition
note: The king’s account names Hezekiah and Jerusalem and describes the pressure placed on Judah. Its first-person royal voice presents Assyrian power and success. Read it as a particular account of the campaign, with an identifiable purpose and perspective.

title: Mark in Codex Sinaiticus
author: Codex Sinaiticus · Mark · project transcription, pinned revision af1633b
role: Manuscript transcription and the project’s description; one witness to a textual question
note: The held transcription ends Mark at 16:8 and records the closing title. The manuscript location is quire 77, folio 5 recto. The project dates the codex to the middle of the fourth century. The later transcription is a modern means of inspecting that ancient witness.
